_about: Factory load catalogue for the Range Day ballistics page. Every number here was read off the maker's page or maker catalogue/ballistics chart (or a retailer reproducing it, marked) on 24 Sep 2026. MV is at the maker's test barrel; the app should let the user override MV from a chrono. bc is the model named in 'model'. 'src' is where the number came from.

_test_barrels.federal_handgun: 4 in (380 Auto 3.75 in; 45 Auto and 10mm 5 in; 5.7x28 4.8 in) — per Federal LE detail pages
_test_barrels.hornady_rifle: 24 in unless noted; 300 BLK 16 in; 7.62x39 20 in; 350 Legend 20 in (InterLock) / 24 in (FTX) / 16 in (Sub-X)
_test_barrels.speer_gold_dot: per 2024 Speer catalog: 380 3.75 in; 38 Spl +P SB 2 in vented; 357 Mag 4 in vented; 40 S&W 3.5-4 in; 45 Auto/10mm 5 in
_test_barrels.federal_rifle: not stated on product pages except where noted (6.5 Grendel Fusion MSR says 24 in); 24 in is the SAAMI convention

10mm.name: 10mm Auto

223.name: .223 Rem
223.about: Commercial .223 (not 5.56 NATO — see the 5.56 set for XM193/XM855). Maker numbers are from a 24" barrel; knock off ~150-200 fps for a 16" gun.

762x39.name: 7.62x39
762x39.about: AK / AR-47. Hornady numbers are from a 20" barrel; Federal doesn't state the barrel. A 16" gun gives up roughly 50-100 fps.

65grendel.name: 6.5 Grendel
65grendel.about: AR-15 cartridge. Maker numbers are from a 24" barrel (Federal says so explicitly); an 18" AR loses ~150 fps, a 16" ~200 fps.

loads.note: 120gr Fusion MSR bonded SP — Federal F65GDLMSR1

6arc.name: 6mm ARC
6arc.about: AR-15 cartridge. Hornady numbers are from a 24" barrel; Hornady's own 18" AR data runs ~100 fps slower, a 16" ~150 fps.

224valk.name: .224 Valkyrie
224valk.about: AR-15 cartridge. Hornady numbers are from a 24" barrel; Federal doesn't state the barrel (their Valkyrie load data uses 24"). Most guns are 18-22".

90gr Sierra MatchKing — Federal Gold Medal GM224VLK1

243.about: Bolt rifle. Maker numbers are from a 24" barrel (Hornady states it; Federal doesn't). A 22" gun loses ~50 fps.

270.name: .270 Win
270.about: Bolt rifle. Maker numbers are from a 24" barrel (Hornady states it; Federal doesn't). A 22" gun loses ~50 fps.

300wm.about: Bolt rifle. Maker numbers are from a 24" barrel (Hornady states it; Federal doesn't). 26" magnums gain ~50-70 fps.

300prc.name: .300 PRC
300prc.about: Bolt rifle. Hornady numbers are from a 24" barrel; most 300 PRC rifles are 24-26".

338lm.name: .338 Lapua
338lm.about: Bolt rifle. Hornady numbers are from a 24" barrel; Federal doesn't state the barrel. Most 338 LM rifles are 26-27" and gain ~50-80 fps.

loads.note: 300gr Sierra MatchKing — Federal Gold Medal GM338LM2

350legend.name: .350 Legend
350legend.about: Straight-wall deer cartridge. Hornady test barrels vary by load (20" InterLock, 24" FTX, 16" Sub-X); Federal doesn't state the barrel. Typical rifles are 16-20".

4570.name: .45-70 Govt
4570.about: Lever gun. Federal and Remington don't state the barrel (24" is the industry convention). Modern 300gr loads are Marlin/Henry-safe; nothing here is a hot Ruger-only load.

12ga.name: 12 ga slug
12ga.about: Slug gun. Federal doesn't state the test barrel on shotshell pages. Foster slugs are for smoothbores; the sabot loads need a rifled barrel.
